assessmentSummary.identity: A four-variant bilateral straight-arm hand-support family requiring explicit selection of quadruped or high-plank base and dynamic retraction-to-protraction cycle or protraction hold. Quadruped retains both hands and knees; high plank retains both hands and toes. Dynamic variants count one complete retraction-to-protraction cycle. Hold variants count actual valid seconds in controlled protraction. Elbow flexion, a full push-up or push-up plus, wall or raised support, knee hover, unilateral or single-leg support, instability, resistance, perturbation, or clinical assessment changes the task.
currentCardFindings: Legacy sources 33, 247, and 853 provide generic or hold skeletons without exact base, action, count, loading, dosage, support, graph, calibration, or review contracts.
The inherited PMID 32707142 citation is a prone cardiopulmonary-resuscitation review and is unrelated to Scapular Push-Ups; it must be removed from current provenance.
Legacy age, publication, outcome, and media implications are unsupported and remain cleared or quarantined.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when exact base, action, count unit, required contacts, straight-arm support, floor access, symptoms, dose, duration, and cumulative wrist, shoulder, pressing, trunk, plank, and downstream hand-support budgets fit. Do not switch base or action silently or add elbow flexion, support height, knee hover, laterality, instability, resistance, perturbation, or assessment. Recompute logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, persistence, and coach and athlete rendering after any change.

calibrationEvidence.basis: Direct Shoulder ABC and ACE instructions, peer-reviewed push-up-plus loading and EMG studies, protraction-hold fatigue context, USA Gymnastics symptom guidance, current oEmbed metadata, and comparison with exact Push-Up and Quadruped Scapular Clock neighbors
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No source validates one universal hand width, scapular range, body line, force, activation, dose, frequency, recovery interval, prevention or treatment result, progression order, or Vortex score. No media candidate has been watched in full.

currentCardSnapshot.description: A four-variant bilateral straight-arm hand-support family that requires exact base and contraction selection. Dynamic variants keep elbows extended while the chest lowers slightly as the scapulae retract, then push the floor away into controlled protraction; one complete retraction-to-protraction cycle is one repetition. Hold variants establish the declared quadruped or high-plank base, push into controlled protraction, and maintain it for measured seconds without elbow motion, body-line loss, shrugging, breath holding, or symptoms. Quadruped uses both hands and knees; high plank uses both hands and toes. A full push-up, push-up plus with elbow flexion, wall or raised support, bear hover, unilateral support, instability, resistance, perturbation, or clinical assessment changes the task.

claims: The exercise sheet describes a push-up position with straight elbows while the shoulder blades are brought together and then pushed forward.
This supports the dynamic straight-arm identity but does not define every Vortex base, hold, count, or graph decision.

evidence.sourceTitle: Exercises to Counteract Too Much Sitting
claims: ACE separates straight-elbow scapular retraction and protraction from an elbow-bending push-up.
Use controlled brace and push terms; the source does not create Vortex taxonomy keys.

evidence.sourceTitle: Serratus Anterior and Upper Trapezius Electromyographic Analysis of the Push-Up Plus Exercise
claims: The review supports serratus anterior and upper-trapezius involvement and reports that setup choices alter EMG findings.
Do not claim isolated activation, quantified force, or one universal muscle pattern for all four variants.

evidence.sourceTitle: Electromyographic Patterns of Scapular Muscles During Four Variations of Protraction–Retraction Exercises
claims: The study explicitly compares quadruped protraction-retraction task conditions.
A small EMG study cannot define universal technique, force, outcome, or dosage.

evidence.sourceTitle: The effects of exercise type and elbow angle on vertical ground reaction force and muscle activity during a push-up plus exercise
claims: Hands-and-feet support produced higher vertical ground reaction force and measured activation than hands-and-knees support.
The 24/18, 32/30, 22/18, and 28/30 proposals describe exercise complexity and physical difficulty only and require independent calibration.

evidence.sourceTitle: Scapula kinematic alterations following a modified push-up plus task
claims: A sustained protraction hold produced measurable fatigue and some scapular kinematic changes in asymptomatic adults.
Track cycles, valid hold and support seconds, faults, symptoms, and overlapping work; recovery and thresholds remain planning estimates.
USA Gymnastics advises medical guidance when pain is present, discontinuing painful exercise, and reducing work when form fails.
Selection requires safe floor entry, exact contacts, clean stable surface, communication, symptom monitoring, and compatible cumulative support exposure.
The programme provides example blocks of two to three sets of eight to ten repetitions or twenty seconds and shows knee lift-off as harder.
Those examples are not universal prescriptions and do not validate Vortex budgets, frequency, or recovery.
The direct instruction keeps elbows straight while the shoulder blades come together and are pushed forward.
Vortex adds exact base, contacts, cycle or hold counting, body-line gates, stops, and persistence without claiming those additions are source-validated outcomes.
The source supports stopping painful exercise and reducing work when form breaks down.
It does not replace facility emergency, trauma, neurologic, circulation, cardiopulmonary, or clinical escalation policy.

evidence.sourceTitle: Multicomponent stretching and rubber band strengthening exercises do not reduce overuse shoulder injuries
claims: The multicomponent programme did not significantly reduce throwing-shoulder overuse prevalence or symptoms.
Do not promise prevention, treatment, readiness, or guaranteed transfer from this exercise.

evidence.sourceTitle: Exercises to Counteract Too Much Sitting
claims: ACE gives concise straight-elbow shoulder-blades-together then apart instruction and identifies elbow bending as a key challenge.
Athlete support must name base and action, show contacts and count unit, and provide clear stop and help signals.

evidence.sourceTitle: Serratus Anterior and Upper Trapezius Electromyographic Analysis of the Push-Up Plus Exercise
claims: Base, hand spacing, elbow angle, shoulder angle, lower-body position, and surface alter observed muscle activity.
Coach support must observe exact setup, first fault, actual exposure, downstream demand, and escalation without diagnosis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Exercises to Counteract Too Much Sitting
claims: ACE demonstrates a related straight-elbow scapular action on stable raised support.
Raised support changes identity, equipment, loading, logistics, and failure consequence and requires a separately authored card.

evidence.sourceTitle: The effects of exercise type and elbow angle on vertical ground reaction force and muscle activity during a push-up plus exercise
claims: Hands-and-knees and hands-and-feet bases create materially different loading while elbow position changes the task.
Keep changed base, elbow action, support height, laterality, stability, resistance, and clinical scope outside the four exact variants until reviewed.
